subject: DI03000091

body.en:
Understand the idea

Atransducer converts a measurand into a related signal;it does not create information or energy without physical interaction.

Explanation and application

  • Choose range,sensitivity,resolution,linearity,hysteresis,repeatability,accuracy/uncertainty and dynamic response for the task.
  • Consider mechanical loading,electrical loading,excitation/self-heating,temperature,moisture,EMI,calibration,maintenance and safety.
  • High sensitivity alone is not enough if the device drifts,saturates,overloads the process or lacks required bandwidth.
Active versus passive?

In this convention,self-generating versus excitation-modulating.

સમજણ અને ઉપયોગ

  • Taskમાટેrange,sensitivity,resolution,linearity,hysteresis,repeatability,accuracy-uncertainty/dynamicresponseલો.
  • Mechanicalloading,electricalloading,excitation-selfheat,T,moisture,EMI,calibration/maintenance-safetyગણો.
  • Highsensitivityમાત્રપૂરતીનથી.Drift,saturation,processloading/bandwidthનીમર્યાદા પણજુઓ.
Active/Passive ફરક?

અહીંselfgenerating/excitation-modulatingનોમુદ્દોછે.

body.en:
Understand the idea

State the classification basis because the same device belongs to several groups.

Explanation and application

  • By electrical phenomenon:resistive,inductive,capacitive,piezoelectric,thermoelectric and other sensing effects.
  • In the usual measurement convention,active/self-generating includes thermocouple and piezoelectric;passive/modulating includes RTD,strain gauge,LVDTand capacitive sensors requiring excitation.
  • By input/application:displacement,strain,force,pressure,temperature,position etc.By output:analogue/discrete or digital-conditioned signals;primary/secondary and contact/non-contact are other bases.
  • "Active sensor"can have a different electronics/network meaning;use the course definition explicitly instead of assuming the word is universal.

body.en:
Definition

Position changes a resistance ratio and hence a measured divider voltage.

Classification / representative type

Passive potentiometric,linear or rotary contact type.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Auniform resistance track and moving wiper define the measured travel.
  2. End terminals connect to a stable approved excitation;wiper feeds a high-input-impedance conditioner.
  3. Mechanical coupling,enclosure and end stops keep travel within rating.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Physical displacement moves the wiper along the track.
  2. Unloaded output Vo≈Vs x/Lfor uniform linear travel;rotation uses an angular ratio.
  3. Conditioning scales the voltage to displacement;finite load resistance distorts this relation.

Applications and interpretation

Position,level mechanisms and controlled low-energy demonstrators.

Limitations and safety

Contact wear,friction,noise and loading limit life/accuracy;never exceed travel or excitation ratings.

body.en:
Definition

Core position changes differential magnetic coupling between an ACprimary and two secondaries.

Classification / representative type

Passive inductive,differential ACtransducer.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. One primary and two symmetrical secondary coils are wound on an insulating former.
  2. An axially movable soft-magnetic core couples flux without sliding electrical contact.
  3. Secondaries connect in series opposition;oscillator,demodulator and conditioner supply excitation and read signed position.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. ACexcitation establishes alternating primary flux;each secondary develops induced voltage.
  2. At geometric null equal secondary voltages oppose;differential output is ideally zero,with possible residual in a real unit.
  3. Core motion increases one coupling and decreases the other;near null Vo≈kxand the180°phase change identifies opposite displacement direction.
  4. Synchronous demodulation produces a signed DCposition signal.The kit DCsupply powers the oscillator;it is not a direct DCexcitation of the LVDTprimary.

Applications and interpretation

Linear position,thickness,force/pressure via a suitable mechanical conversion.

Limitations and safety

Limited linear range,temperature/excitation effects and alignment errors require calibration;do not treat all travel as linear.

body.en:
Definition

Rotating magnetic geometry changes differential coupling and gives an angular position signal.

Classification / representative type

Passive inductive rotary differential transducer.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Primary and differential secondary windings form the ACmagnetic assembly.
  2. Rotary core/rotor has a shaped magnetic profile linked to the measured shaft.
  3. ACexcitation,demodulator and mechanical reference establish zero and scale.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Excitation creates alternating coupling flux.
  2. Rotation shifts secondary coupling balance around the null.
  3. Within the rated linear angular sector,conditioned output is approximately proportional to signed angle;it is not automatically a360°absolute encoder.

Applications and interpretation

Shaft-angle feedback and limited-angle actuator position.

Limitations and safety

Observe angular limits,excitation and coupling requirements;do not substitute a resistive rotary potentiometer model.

body.en:
Definition

The measured quantity changes plate area,separation or dielectric permittivity.

Classification / representative type

Passive capacitive,contact or non-contact depending on design.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Two conducting electrodes and an insulating dielectric form capacitance.
  2. Geometry allows motion,gap,overlap or dielectric change with the measurand.
  3. Shielded leads,guarding and a suitable ACbridge/oscillator conditioner resolve small changes.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. For ideal parallel plates,C=εA/dwith fringing neglected.
  2. Increasing area/permittivity raises C;increasing gap lowers C.Near a small gap change,ΔC/C≈−Δd/d.
  3. Conditioning converts Cchange into a voltage/frequency/position output after calibration.

Applications and interpretation

Displacement,pressure diaphragms,level and material/proximity sensing.

Limitations and safety

Stray C,humidity,dielectric variation and fringing matter;use the rated geometry and guard practice.

body.en:
Definition

Stress on a suitable crystal/ceramic creates charge;mechanical energy is converted to electrical signal.

Classification / representative type

Active/self-generating,piezoelectric force/vibration type.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Piezoelectric crystal/ceramic,electrodes and force-transfer structure form the sensing element.
  2. Case,preload and insulation protect fragile material and establish a rated load path.
  3. High-input-Zor charge amplifier,screened cable and mounting interface preserve small charge signals.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Applied changing force creates charge Q≈dFfor the stated sensitivity d.
  2. Open-circuit-like signal V≈Q/Ctotal;leakage and input resistance give a finite discharge time constant.
  3. Charge conditioning measures dynamic force/vibration;static signals decay,so it is not generally a sustained DCforce sensor or free-energy generator.

Applications and interpretation

Vibration,impact,dynamic pressure and carefully designed mechanical-energy harvesting demonstrations.

Limitations and safety

Fragility,leakage,mounting resonance and overload matter;harvested energy comes from mechanical work.

body.en:
Definition

Elastic strain changes conductor resistance;strain ε=ΔL/Lis dimensionless.

Classification / representative type

Passive resistive,bonded wire/foil or unbonded wire type.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Bonded foil/wire grid is attached through insulating backing and adhesive to the test surface.
  2. Unbonded fine wires are stretched between insulated frames;relative frame motion strains the wires.
  3. Lead wires,protective coating,Wheatstone bridge and amplifier provide measurement and temperature compensation.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Applied load deforms the specimen or frame within its elastic limit.
  2. Gauge factor GF=(ΔR/R)/εrelates resistance change to strain.
  3. Aquarter bridge with one active arm gives |Vo|≈Vs GF|ε|/4for small strain;polarity depends on arm and output order.
  4. Example:R120Ω,GF2,ε1000µstrain gives ΔR0.24Ω;at5Vexcitation ideal quarter-bridge magnitude≈2.5mV.

Applications and interpretation

Load cells,force/pressure beams and structural strain.

Limitations and safety

Bond quality,temperature,lead resistance,creep and self-heating require control;do not overload the specimen.

body.en:
Definition

Atemperature difference in a circuit of dissimilar conductors produces thermoelectric emf.

Classification / representative type

Active/self-generating thermoelectric transducer.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Two appropriate dissimilar alloys form the sensing/hot junction.
  2. Insulation,sheath and extension/compensation leads suit the temperature,environment and thermocouple type.
  3. Cold-junction compensation and a high-impedance millivolt instrument convert emfusing the correct type table.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Measured emfE=f(Th)−f(Tc),not an absolute hot-junction temperature by itself.
  2. Within a small range E≈S(Th−Tc),but sensitivity is nonlinear over large ranges;use the correct type/polarity and reference compensation.
  3. Illustrative S40µV/KandΔT100Kgive4mV;this is a constant-Sexample,not an exact universal type-Ktable.

Applications and interpretation

Furnaces,machine parts and wide-temperature industrial sensing with suitable installation.

Limitations and safety

Hot surfaces,polarity,type mismatch,ground loops and poor junction compensation create hazards/errors;no unprotected hot-surface handling.

body.en:
Definition

Metal resistance changes predictably with temperature;platinum is widely used.

Classification / representative type

Passive resistive temperature detector.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Wire-wound or thin-film metal sensing element is mounted on an insulating support.
  2. Protective sheath and leads provide mechanical/environmental protection.
  3. Controlled small excitation and two/three/four-wire readout are selected for lead-error and accuracy requirements.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Excitation produces a resistance-related voltage.
  2. Near the declared reference,R≈R0[1+α(T−T0)];wide-range precision requires the appropriate nonlinear relation.
  3. Illustration:Pt100with R0=100Ωat0°C,α0.00385/°C gives about138.5Ωat100°Cin the linear model.

Applications and interpretation

Accurate process temperature where suitable range,response and calibration are provided.

Limitations and safety

Self-heating and lead resistance matter;three-wire compensation assumes suitable lead matching,four-wire separates current/potential paths.

  1. Insulatingsupportપરwire-woundકેthin-filmmetalelementહોય.
  2. Sheath/leadsmechanical-environmentalprotectionઆપે.
  3. Leaderror-accuracyમુજબsmallcontrolledexcitation/two-three-fourwirereadoutપસંદથાય.

Working — ક્રમ અને કારણ

  1. ExcitationથીR-relatedVમળે.
  2. DeclaredreferenceપાસેR≈R0[1+α(T−T0)]છે.Wide-rangeprecisionમાંpropernonlinearrelationજોઈએ.
  3. IllustrationમાંPt100નું0°CએR0=100Ω/α0.00385/°Cહોયતોlinearmodelમાં100°Cએલગભગ138.5Ωછે.

body.en:
Definition

Asemiconductor resistance changes strongly with temperature,usually decreasing for NTCtypes.

Classification / representative type

Passive resistive,NTCor PTCaccording to the device.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Semiconductor bead,disc or chip is enclosed for the intended thermal/contact environment.
  2. Leads and a low-power divider/bridge provide resistance measurement.
  3. Calibration table or model and conditioner convert nonlinear resistance to temperature.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Sensing element approaches the measured temperature after its thermal settling time.
  2. For an NTCbeta approximation,R=R0 exp[β(1/T−1/T0)],with T and T0in kelvin.
  3. Read with small enough power to avoid self-heating and apply the actual device calibration;PTCdoes not follow this NTCequation blindly.

Applications and interpretation

Temperature compensation,alarms,thermal control and inrush applications for specifically rated types.

Limitations and safety

High sensitivity comes with nonlinearity,limited range and interchangeability/self-heating errors.
body.gu:

Understand the idea

Detect approach/presence without intended mechanical contact,using a rated sensing principle.

Explanation and application

  • Inductive types sense conductive/metal targets through field/eddy-current effects;capacitive types detect dielectric changes and can sense suitable non-metallic materials.
  • Optical/photoelectric and magnetic types use different targets/geometry;range,target material,mounting and contamination determine reliability.
  • Know normally-open/closed and PNP/NPNor analogue output,voltage/current rating and controller input;an output signal is not a power connection for an arbitrary load.
  • Use approved low-voltage trainers to test approach/release distance,hysteresis and repeatability;do not bypass machine interlocks with an unverified sensor.

LVDTlinear displacement

Use the approved rated trainer,instruments/references and manufacturer manual;no physical experiment is claimed.

Approved low-voltage LVDTkit:oscillator drives primary AC;series-opposed secondaries feed the specified demodulator/readout.

Qualified-supervised procedure

Fit sensitivity ΔVo/Δxover the linear region;check zero,residual,linearity and return repeatability.

Kit DCpowers electronics,not bare primary DC;misaligned core or wrong secondary opposition causes errors.

No CTsecondary open under primary current;no PTsecondary short;no arbitrary insulation voltage or defeated earth.Scope grounds remain PE/common;never lift PEor float an earthed scope.Use approved rated differential/isolated-input methods if needed.

Aim and apparatus

Strain measurement by strain gauge

Use the approved rated trainer,instruments/references and manufacturer manual;no physical experiment is claimed.

Connections and instruments

Use a rated elastic test beam/gauge/bridge/amplifier trainer with stable approved excitation and reference loading.

Qualified-supervised procedure

  1. Identify ratings,ranges,terminals,test conditions and stop criteria;prepare an approved diagram and reference/uncertainty plan.

GF=(ΔR/R)/ε;for the declared quarter bridge |Vo|≈Vs GF|ε|/4;use actual gauge factor and calibration.
